content:
**save reports what it did (#637)**

plainfiles.save appends the durable record and THEN rebuilds the index, and cannot be ordered otherwise because rebuildIndex reads the whole store. When the rebuild refuses on a pre-existing tampered record, the operator was told 'plainfiles.save() failed' while the record was already on disk. Ruled option 1 (report accurately) and rejected 2 and 3 on the ticket's own ground: save must not refuse the operator's valid record because of somebody else's broken one. Measured the retry and it is worse than the ticket says -- ts is hashed into the content-addressed id at second resolution, so three retries produced three DISTINCT ids; only a same-second retry duplicates an id, while every hand retry mints a record no dedup can ever collapse. Built the readRecordIds dedup that dualWriteRecords already has (#221), measured it, and REMOVED it: it can only fire on a same-second retry, memory:save has no automated caller, and shipping a guard that reads as protection and cannot fire is #632's shape -- a green that means nothing. Cost measured before deciding: readRecordIds 96ms vs rebuildIndex 336ms on 2046 records. The error is annotated and rethrown rather than wrapped so rebuildIndex's file:line diagnosis and the stack survive, and cli.mjs keys on a flag set at exactly one site so a pre-append refusal cannot reach the new branch. The prescribed recovery is executed in a test, not just asserted as wording.
